BiblicalUsage: This Aramaic word means length, and it is used for the lengthening of a king's peace and the lengthening of beasts' lives. Daniel tells Nebuchadnezzar his tranquillity may be lengthened if he breaks off his sins, and the beasts of his later vision have their dominion taken away yet their lives prolonged for a season.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for length carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the mercy in it, that God lengthens days even for kings and beasts, and gives time to turn.
